page.home.faq.heading: Frequently asked <secondary>questions</secondary>
page.home.faq.meshtastic.a: A storage and data layer for Meshtastic networks and telemetry data. The data comes from MQTT and gets stored and processed in Mesh Things. Mesh Things can be deployed locally on a Raspberry Pi or on a cloud server.
page.home.faq.federated.q: Can data be shared across instances?
page.home.faq.federated.a: Yes, you can keep data local or send it to a cloud server.
page.home.faq.globe.a: Yes, we are working on releasing the platform and it's front-end application. Stay tuned for more news, and feel free to contact us for more information.
page.home.faq.signIn.a: Anyone can register an owner account in the demo server. Storage of data in the demo server is not guaranteed yet. Feel free to contact us for more information and deployment options.

page.terms.tou.accepting.body: These Terms apply to anyone who uses the Platform. page.terms.tou.platform.heading: 4. The Mesh Things Platform
page.terms.tou.platform.body: Mesh Things is a storage and console layer for Meshtastic networks: it lets you register meshes and devices, ingest telemetry, and configure alarms and blueprints through the console. You're responsible for the Meshtastic devices and networks you connect to it. api.sensical.es and things.sensical.es are a demo instance of Mesh Things.
page.terms.tou.account.heading: 5. Creating an owner account
page.terms.tou.account.body: To use the console you need to create an owner account with a name, email address and password. If you suspect unauthorized use of your account, change your password immediately and notify Sensical at info@sensical.es.
page.terms.tou.usingPlatform.heading: 6. Using the Platform and registering mesh data
page.terms.tou.usingPlatform.body: If you register meshes, devices or telemetry under your account, you're responsible for the accuracy and legality of that data and for the devices you connect. For the personal data in that traffic, and in what you forward through sinks, you act as controller, as set out in the Data Processing Agreement. Sensical doesn't screen or verify device data before storing it, and storing it doesn't make Sensical liable for its content or accuracy.
page.terms.tou.accessingData.heading: 7. Accessing mesh and device data
page.terms.tou.accessingData.body: Meshes and devices you register are private to your account unless you choose otherwise: only you and the accounts you give access to can read their configuration and telemetry. If you make a mesh public, every signed-in account can read its devices and telemetry, including positions, but can't see its channel key or change anything. Visitors who aren't signed in can't. If you're an operator, you can also forward readings and alarms to sinks you create, and whoever holds a sink's credentials receives them. Sensical's administrators can access every mesh, only to operate, support and secure the service. Sensical doesn't sell your mesh data or share it with anyone beyond the sub-processors listed in the Data Processing Agreement and the recipients of the sinks you create.
page.terms.tou.platformChanges.heading: 8. Changes to the Platform

It will email you at least 30 days before it removes a feature you use or tightens limits on storage, request rates or API usage, unless a change is needed sooner for security or legal reasons. If a change affects data already stored, you'll be able to export it before the change takes effect.
page.terms.tou.termination.heading: 9. Termination
page.terms.tou.termination.body: You may delete your account at any time from the console profile page. Your account and its access are removed at once. The data of your meshes and sources is deleted 30 days later and removed from backups within a further 7 days. Export any data you want to keep before deleting your account. Sensical keeps a record of the terms you accepted and the archive and sink instructions you gave, with your name and email address, for 5 years after your account is deleted, to show that it processed data as you instructed. Sensical may suspend or close accounts that violate these Terms or otherwise abuse the service, and will try to notify you by email beforehand where practical; the same deletion periods then apply.

page.terms.privacy.heading: Privacy Policy
page.terms.privacy.intro: This Privacy Policy explains what personal data Mesh Things collects about you and why. Read it together with the Terms of Use above.
page.terms.privacy.purpose.heading: 1. Purpose of this Privacy Policy
page.terms.privacy.purpose.body: This Privacy Policy covers the personal data Sensical processes as controller when you use the Platform: your account and how you use it. The data of the meshes, sources and sinks you set up is processed by Sensical on your behalf, as your processor, under the Data Processing Agreement rather than this policy. Terms defined in the Terms of Use above have the same meaning here.
page.terms.privacy.changesPrivacy.body: Sensical may update this Privacy Policy as the Platform evolves. It will email you at least 30 days before a material change takes effect, and the current version, with its effective date, is always on this page. If you disagree with a change, you can close your account before it takes effect.
page.terms.privacy.dataProcessed.heading: 3. Personal data Sensical processes
page.terms.privacy.dataProcessed.body: Your name and email address; your password (stored only as hashes); your settings; your API keys (stored only as hashes); a session cookie while you're signed in; a record of each set of terms you accept, with its version, the time and your name and email address; the archive and sink instructions you give, with the same details; and what you write to Sensical when you ask for support. Your name, email address and password are needed to create an account; without them Sensical can't provide one.
page.terms.privacy.processingPurposes.bo: Sensical uses your account data to create and maintain your account, run the console and send service emails, such as verification, password reset, alarms, the source and sink status alerts you turn on, and terms renewal notices, because this is necessary to provide the Platform you signed up for (Article 6(1)(b) GDPR). It keeps the records of terms accepted and instructions given to show that it complies with data protection law and to defend itself against claims (Article 6(1)(c) and (f)). It uses technical data, such as your IP address, to secure the service and prevent abuse, for example by limiting sign-in attempts, based on its legitimate interest in keeping the Platform safe (Article 6(1)(f)). Sensical makes no automated decisions about you. The marketing site sets no analytics cookies, and the console only sets a session cookie once you sign in, so the API knows who you are.
page.terms.privacy.dataSharing.heading: 5. Who receives your data
page.terms.privacy.dataSharing.body: Sensical doesn't sell or rent your personal data. Its hosting provider, Hetzner (Germany and Finland), its email provider, Scaleway (France), and the provider of its info@sensical.es mailbox, EuroDNS (Luxembourg), process it on Sensical's behalf. Other signed-in accounts can see your name, in the owner directory and on the meshes you make public or share with them. Otherwise Sensical only shares your data when you've asked it to, when needed to investigate abuse or enforce these Terms, or when required by law.
page.terms.privacy.retention.heading: 6. How long Sensical keeps your data
page.terms.privacy.retention.body: Your account data is kept while your account exists. When you delete your account, it is removed at once, and from backups within 7 days. The records of terms you accepted and instructions you gave are kept for 5 years after your account is deleted, the period in which claims can usually be brought, and then deleted. Support emails are kept for as long as needed to answer you and follow up. Technical logs, which can include your IP address, are deleted after 30 days.
page.terms.privacy.yourRights.heading: 9. Your rights
page.terms.privacy.yourRights.body: You have the right to access your personal data, to have it corrected or erased, to restrict or object to its processing, and to receive it in a portable format. You can see and correct your details, and delete your account, from the console profile page. For anything else, write to info@sensical.es; Sensical answers within one month. If you think Sensical hasn't respected your rights, you can complain to the Spanish Data Protection Agency (AEPD, www.aepd.es).
page.terms.privacy.yourNode.heading: 10. If your node appears on Mesh Things
page.terms.privacy.yourNode.body: Mesh Things stores data from the Meshtastic nodes that reach the meshes and sources its users set up, which can include nodes of people who have no account here. For that data, the owner of the mesh or source is the controller and decides what is collected and why; Sensical processes it only on their behalf. If you think data from your node is stored here, write to info@sensical.es with your node's ID. Sensical will pass your request to the owner concerned and help them answer it.
page.terms.privacy.dataStorage.heading: 7. Where your data is stored
page.terms.privacy.dataStorage.body: Sensical stores your data on servers in the European Union and doesn't transfer it outside the European Economic Area. When you view a map, though, your browser loads map tiles and map code directly from CARTO, OpenFreeMap and unpkg. Those services receive your IP address and may serve the request from outside the European Union, under their own privacy policies.
page.terms.privacy.security.heading: 8. Security of your data
page.terms.privacy.security.body: Sensical takes reasonable steps to protect your data, including transport encryption and access controls, but no transmission over the internet is completely secure. page.terms.dpa.heading: Data Processing Agreement
page.terms.dpa.body: For the mesh, source and sink data you bring into the Platform, you are the controller and Sensical processes it only on your behalf. page.dpa.title: Data Processing Agreement
page.dpa.toc.heading: Contents
page.dpa.intro: This Data Processing Agreement ("DPA") forms part of the Mesh Things Terms of Use. It is agreed between Sensical SCCL, CIF ESF27637909, Diputació 151, 08011 Barcelona, Spain ("Sensical"), as processor, and each owner who accepts the terms of a mesh, a source or a sink ("you"), as controller, under Article 28 of the General Data Protection Regulation (EU) 2016/679 ("GDPR"). You accept it when you accept a mesh's, a source's or a sink's terms, and the version you accepted is recorded with that acceptance.
page.dpa.agreement.heading: Agreement
page.dpa.annexes.heading: Annexes
page.dpa.annexes.intro: The annexes describe the processing, the security measures and the sub-processors. Sensical may update them as described in sections 6 and 8 without you accepting this DPA again.
page.dpa.subject.heading: 1. Subject matter and duration
page.dpa.subject.p1: Sensical processes personal data on your behalf only to provide the Mesh Things service for the meshes, sources and sinks you set up: to receive, decrypt, decode, store, display, export and delete the traffic your meshes and sources bring in, and to forward it to the sinks you create, as described in Annex I.
page.dpa.subject.p2: This DPA applies while you have a mesh, a source or a sink whose terms you accepted, and afterwards for as long as Sensical still holds its data under section 11. It ends with the Terms of Use. Your statutory rights are unaffected.
page.dpa.roles.heading: 2. Roles
page.dpa.roles.p1: For the data described in Annex I you are the controller and Sensical is the processor. You are responsible for the lawfulness of the processing, including having a lawful basis and informing the people whose nodes appear on your mesh, as you confirm when you accept the mesh or source terms.
page.dpa.roles.p2: For your own account data (name, email address and password), Sensical is the controller, and the Privacy Policy covers that data.
page.dpa.instructions.heading: 3. Your instructions
page.dpa.instructions.p1: Sensical processes the data only on your documented instructions, unless EU or Member State law requires otherwise. In that case Sensical tells you first, unless that law forbids it.
page.dpa.instructions.p2: Your instructions are this DPA and what you configure in the service: the gateways and sources you register, the devices you archive, the sinks you create and the meshes and devices you attach to them, the alarms and blueprints you set, whether a mesh is public, and the accounts you give access to. Sensical records who turned archiving on or off for each device and who attached or detached each mesh and device from a sink, and when.
page.dpa.instructions.sinks: When you attach meshes or devices to a sink, Sensical publishes their readings and alarms, in the streams you choose, on its own broker, where whoever holds that sink's credentials can subscribe to them. The recipients of a sink are yours, not Sensical's sub-processors: you choose them and give them the credentials, and you are responsible for their use of the data, including any transfer outside the European Economic Area. A sink keeps no data of its own, and deleting it or detaching its meshes and devices stops the forwarding.
page.dpa.instructions.p3: You can give further instructions by email to info@sensical.es. If Sensical believes an instruction breaks data protection law, it will tell you and may suspend it until you confirm or change it.
page.dpa.location.heading: 4. Location and transfers
page.dpa.location.p1: Sensical processes and stores the data only in the European Union or the European Economic Area. A transfer outside it requires your prior authorisation through the procedure in section 8, and takes place only with a safeguard under Chapter V GDPR, such as an adequacy decision or the EU standard contractual clauses.
page.dpa.confidentiality.heading: 5. Confidentiality
page.dpa.confidentiality.p1: Only people who need access to run the service can access the data. They are bound by confidentiality, which continues after their work for Sensical ends. Sensical's administrators access mesh data only to operate, support and secure the service.
page.dpa.security.heading: 6. Security
page.dpa.security.p1: Sensical implements the technical and organisational measures in Annex II, appropriate to the risk as required by Article 32 GDPR.
page.dpa.security.p2: The measures follow technical progress. Sensical may change them as long as the overall level of protection does not fall, and publishes the current Annex II on this page. Such a change does not require you to accept this DPA again.
page.dpa.assistance.heading: 7. Assistance
page.dpa.assistance.p1: Taking into account the nature of the processing, Sensical helps you answer requests from data subjects to exercise their rights, mainly through the service itself: you can view, export and delete your meshes' data. If a data subject contacts Sensical directly about your mesh, Sensical forwards the request to you without undue delay and does not answer it on your behalf unless you ask.
page.dpa.assistance.p2: With the information available to it, Sensical also helps you with security, breach notification, data protection impact assessments and prior consultation of a supervisory authority (Articles 32 to 36 GDPR).
page.dpa.subprocessors.heading: 8. Sub-processors
page.dpa.subprocessors.p1: You give Sensical general authorisation to engage sub-processors. The current ones are listed in Annex III. Sensical binds each of them by contract to data protection obligations equivalent to this DPA and remains fully liable to you for their performance.
page.dpa.subprocessors.p2: Sensical tells you by email, and on this page, at least 30 days before adding or replacing a sub-processor. You may object on reasonable data protection grounds within that period. If the objection can't be resolved, you can end the processing before the change takes effect by deleting the affected meshes and sources, or your account.
page.dpa.breaches.heading: 9. Personal data breaches
page.dpa.breaches.p1: Sensical notifies you without undue delay, and in any case within 48 hours, after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting your data. The notice describes, as far as known, the nature of the breach, the categories and approximate number of data subjects and records concerned, its likely consequences, the measures taken or proposed, and a contact point. Sensical adds information as it becomes available.
page.dpa.audits.heading: 10. Information and audits
page.dpa.audits.p1: Sensical makes available the information needed to demonstrate compliance with Article 28 GDPR, including this DPA, Annex II and its hosting provider's certifications. You may audit Sensical yourself or through an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, once a year, with 30 days' notice, during business hours and without disrupting the service. Each party bears its own costs, unless the audit reveals a material breach of this DPA by Sensical.
page.dpa.deletion.heading: 11. Deletion and return
page.dpa.deletion.p1: You can export your meshes' data at any time, including the Parquet archive of archived devices or via the API. When you delete a mesh or a source, when its terms lapse without renewal, or when you delete your account, Sensical deletes the related data after the grace period stated in those terms, unless you renew in the meantime or EU or Member State law requires it to be kept.
page.dpa.deletion.p2: Backups are overwritten on rotation, within 7 days of the data being deleted from the service. Sensical keeps the records needed to prove proper processing, such as terms acceptances and archive and sink instructions, for 5 years after your account is deleted, and uses them for no other purpose.
page.dpa.liability.heading: 12. Liability
page.dpa.liability.p1: Each party's liability under this DPA follows the Terms of Use. Nothing in this DPA limits either party's liability to data subjects under Article 82 GDPR.
page.dpa.changes.heading: 13. Changes and other terms
page.dpa.changes.p1: Sensical may update this DPA to reflect changes in the law or the service. Changes to sections 1 to 13 are announced by email at least 30 days before they take effect, and you accept them by renewing your mesh and source terms. Changes to the annexes follow sections 6 and 8. Each version is dated, and earlier versions are available on request.
page.dpa.changes.p2: On data protection, this DPA prevails over the Terms of Use. It is governed by Spanish law and the courts of Barcelona have jurisdiction, except where mandatory law provides otherwise. If any provision is invalid, the rest remain in force.
page.dpa.annex1.heading: Annex I. Details of the processing
page.dpa.annex1.purpose.heading: Subject matter and purpose
page.dpa.annex1.purpose.p1: Providing Mesh Things for your meshes, sources and sinks: receiving traffic from your gateways on the default broker or from the brokers your sources bridge, decrypting it with the keys you provide, decoding and storing it, showing it in the console and the API, computing blueprints and alarms, emailing alarms, archiving the devices you choose, forwarding readings and alarms to the sinks you create, and exporting and deleting it.
page.dpa.annex1.nature.heading: Nature of the processing
page.dpa.annex1.nature.p1: Collection, decryption, decoding, storage, structuring, consultation, disclosure to the accounts you authorise and to the recipients of your sinks, transmission by email, export and erasure. The processing is automated and takes no decisions about individuals.
page.dpa.annex1.data.heading: Categories of personal data
page.dpa.annex1.data.li1: Device identifiers: node numbers, long and short names, hardware model and gateway IDs.
page.dpa.annex1.data.li2: Location data: positions reported by nodes, with their precision and time.
page.dpa.annex1.data.li3: Telemetry: device metrics, such as battery and channel use, and sensor readings, such as environment, air quality and power.
page.dpa.annex1.data.li4: Data derived from the above: data processing results for calibration and correction purposes, alarms and data quality events.
page.dpa.annex1.subjects.heading: Data subjects
page.dpa.annex1.subjects.li1: People who own or operate nodes whose traffic reaches your mesh or source, including people with no Mesh Things account.
page.dpa.annex1.subjects.li2: You and the people you give access to your meshes, where the service records their actions.
page.dpa.annex1.special.heading: Special categories
page.dpa.annex1.special.p1: None intended. You undertake not to use the service to collect special categories of data or to track or profile individuals.
page.dpa.annex1.duration.heading: Duration
page.dpa.annex1.duration.p1: While the mesh, source or sink is in use and its terms are valid, plus the deletion grace period and backup rotation in section 11.
page.dpa.annex2.heading: Annex II. Technical and organisational measures
page.dpa.annex2.hosting.heading: Hosting and physical security
page.dpa.annex2.hosting.li1: Servers run in Hetzner data centres in the EU, with physical access control, video surveillance, redundant power and cooling, and fire protection, certified under ISO/IEC 27001.
page.dpa.annex2.network.heading: Network and servers
page.dpa.annex2.network.li1: A host firewall exposes only SSH and the service's public endpoints. Databases, message queues and internal services are not reachable from the internet.
page.dpa.annex2.network.li2: SSH accepts keys only, with no root login, and repeated failed attempts are blocked.
page.dpa.annex2.network.li3: All public endpoints use TLS. Administration interfaces sit behind password authentication at the proxy.
page.dpa.annex2.network.li5: Access to the hosting provider's console requires two-factor authentication.
page.dpa.annex2.access.heading: Access control in the service
page.dpa.annex2.access.li1: Passwords and API keys are stored only as hashes. New accounts must confirm their email address, and sign-in and sign-up are rate-limited.
page.dpa.annex2.access.li2: Role-based permissions (owner, operator, administrator) decide who can read and change each mesh. Meshes are private unless their owner makes them public.
page.dpa.annex2.access.li3: Channel and admin keys are returned only to the mesh's owner.
page.dpa.annex2.access.li4: The Parquet archive is read with temporary credentials limited to one mesh.
page.dpa.annex2.access.li5: Each sink has its own credentials, generated by Sensical, that can only subscribe to that sink's readings. When a sink's terms lapse, it is paused and its credentials are refused.
page.dpa.annex2.separation.heading: Separation and minimisation
page.dpa.annex2.separation.li1: Readings are tagged and partitioned by mesh, and every query is scoped to what the caller may see.
page.dpa.annex2.separation.li2: Only traffic from registered gateways and sources is stored. Archiving is off by default and enabled per device.
page.dpa.annex2.separation.li3: When terms lapse, ingestion stops before anything is deleted, and deletions are scheduled, retried and logged. In-flight messages are kept for at most 7 days.
page.dpa.annex2.separation.li4: Service logs, which can include IP addresses, are deleted after 30 days.
page.dpa.annex2.availability.heading: Availability and recovery
page.dpa.annex2.availability.li1: Servers are backed up daily with Hetzner's backup service, which keeps the last 7 backups in Hetzner's EU data centres.
page.dpa.annex2.organisation.heading: Organisation
page.dpa.annex2.organisation.li1: Access to production is limited to the Sensical staff who run the service, bound by confidentiality.
page.dpa.annex2.organisation.li2: Terms acceptances and archive and sink instructions are recorded with who gave them and when.
page.dpa.annex2.organisation.li3: Breaches are handled under a documented incident procedure that meets section 9, and every breach is recorded. These measures are reviewed at least once a year and whenever the service changes significantly.
page.dpa.annex3.heading: Annex III. Sub-processors
page.dpa.annex3.intro: Sensical uses the following sub-processors. None of them processes the data outside the EU.
